chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who applies depilatory lime, then mixes flour with oil, kneads it with it, and rubs himself with it after the depilatory in order to remove its odor. He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الدَّقِيقَ: flour, mentioned here as a substance mixed with oil
key_terms.الزَّيْتِ: oil used to mix with the flour
key_terms.النُّورَةِ: depilatory lime used for hair removal
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَطَّلِي: applies a depilatory substance to the body

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use flour mixed with oil after applying depilatory lime to remove its odor?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no harm in using flour mixed with oil on the body after applying depilatory lime in order to remove its smell. Its significance in this chapter is to distinguish such bodily use of flour from using flour for tayammum, which is not permitted.
